related_questions.snippet: What does the Raise the Wage Act of 2025 do? The federal minimum hourly wage is just $7.25 and has not increased since 2009. related_questions.question: What states are going to $15 an hour minimum wage?

text_blocks.snippet: Several states will reach or have already reached a $15 per hour minimum wage in 2025. These include California, Connecticut, Delaware, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Oregon, Rhode Island, and Washington. Additionally, Florida, Missouri, and Nebraska are on track to reach $15 in the coming years.

related_questions.question: Is executive order 14026 still in effect?

text_blocks.snippet: No, Executive Order 14026 is no longer in effect. It was rescinded by President Trump on March 14, 2025, as part of a broader revocation of several Biden-era executive orders. The order had previously raised the minimum wage for federal contractors to $15 per hour, with subsequent annual increases.
snippet_highlighted_words: No, Executive Order 14026 is no longer in effect

list.title: Original Order:
list.snippet: Executive Order 14026, signed by President Biden, mandated a $15 per hour minimum wage for federal contractors, with adjustments for inflation.

list.title: Rescission:
list.snippet: President Trump revoked this order on March 14, 2025.

list.title: Impact:
list.snippet: The rescission effectively eliminated the $15 minimum wage for federal contractors established by the order.

list.title: Current Situation:
list.snippet: Federal contractors must now adhere to the minimum wage standards set by state or local laws, or their collective bargaining agreements, if applicable.
